rationale: Objective: minimize latency_ms of one complete offline batch=32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward (model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode()). Baseline latency_ms=4.237417 (project.json original_baseline; revision f2cfe831 has no installed bundles, so requires/replaces are empty). Evidence: execution_timeline-1221e205 shows 88 kernels with kernel_active_union_us=4066.6 vs gaps_between_kernels_us=81.1 on one serial stream (compute_overlap_us=0.0), i.e. GPU-compute-bound, so only removing serial GPU kernel time moves latency; leaf diagnostics attribute 3043.1us to aten::conv2d (20), 428.5us to aten::batch_norm (20), 341.9us to aten::relu (17), 200.1us to max_pool2d, 121.0us to add_. Strategy: all 20 selected conv sites (17 ResNetConvLayer + 3 ResNetShortCut module calls) run with training=False and a frozen eval-mode BatchNorm2d directly after a bias-free conv (observed conv2d signatures have bias=None), so each conv+BN pair collapses exactly into one F.conv2d(x, W', b') with scale=gamma/sqrt(running_var+eps), W'=W*scale, b'=beta-scale*running_mean, followed by the site's unchanged activation module call (ReLU/Identity; shortcuts have none). This removes all 20 aten::batch_norm kernels (428.5us of serial leaf time, ~10.5% of the busy union) while every aten::conv2d kernel still executes (now with a negligible per-channel bias epilogue), and all aten::relu/max_pool2d/add_ work continues in surviving parents. Selecting all 20 module calls as one joint bundle keeps the policy coherent (partial folding would mix eager BN with folded sites); each edit is a direct module callable boundary under the legacy binding backend, so no functional dispatch overhead is added on unrelated operators. Fidelity: pure FP32 fold arithmetic; TF32 stays disabled, no autocast/quantization/cudnn.benchmark change; the transform is algebraically exact for eval-mode BN up to FP32 rounding. The selection records CPU pre-validation with the exact frozen weights and the exact batch=32 workload input: max_abs_err=7.6e-6 over the full 1000-class logits vs the atol=rtol=1e-4 budget (0/32000 violations), exact top-1 preserved (min top1-top2 margin 0.1446, four orders above the error), warm cached path bit-stable across repeated invocations; this remains a hypothesis until the framework's independent GPU validation confirms quality and wall latency. No previous-feedback.txt or previous-candidate exists at this revision (first attempt). Runtime policy: the replacement takes the folded path only for the observed signature class (single 4-D float32 CUDA tensor on the folded weights' device with matching in_channels, modules in eval, grad disabled, no extra args) and otherwise re-enters the untouched parent forward, so unsupported signatures, a flipped training flag or an unexpected grad-enabled caller cannot corrupt outputs; route labels are self-reported via context['record_route'] ('bn_folded_conv2d', 'fallback:signature', 'fallback:fold_setup_failed') as diagnostics only. Every invocation executes the real conv kernels on the current inputs: no output caching, no fixture precomputation, no CUDA Graph capture (Python replacement invocations remain observable for coverage). Eliminated calls: the 40 inner module boundaries (20 ...convolution Conv2d + 20 ...normalization BatchNorm2d calls) and the 20 aten.batch_norm.default functional calls under them. Their consumers remain valid because each replacement returns a tensor with the same shape, dtype, device and (up to fold rounding) values as the parent conv->BN output: downstream max_pool2d, stage/residual add_ and subsequent layers consume unchanged tensors; aten::conv2d kernels still run inside the replacements via F.conv2d; aten::relu still runs through the unchanged activation modules; the profiler record_function annotations that instrumented the removed conv/bn module boundaries are observation instrumentation and disappear with those boundaries during profiled recapture, which does not affect outputs. Expected effect: latency_ms ~4.24 -> ~3.8 (-8..-11%); images_per_second is the exact reciprocal at fixed batch and rises proportionally, keeping the offline row's 0.95 memory-goal throughput ratio satisfied.

setup_work.when: build(context) (installation; before quality tracking and before the adapter's invocation starts). No per-invocation setup: folded tensors are computed once and reused; adapter.reset() only calls model.eval(), and eval-mode parameters of this inference-only warm-model lifecycle are invariant across invocations.
actions: For each of the 20 selected module sites: read conv.weight (bias is None at every site), bn.weight/bias/running_mean/running_var/eps, and compute scale=gamma/sqrt(var+eps), W'=W*scale (per out-channel), b'=beta-scale*running_mean under torch.no_grad() on the model's CUDA device, then .contiguous(). Roughly 20 small elementwise setup kernels plus 20 tiny reductions, executed once at install.

Capture (W', b'), stride/padding/dilation/groups and the activation module reference in per-site closures; no model parameter, buffer or module attribute is mutated (the parent forward and its parameters stay intact for guarded fallback); no module.forward wrapper is installed by the candidate; no CUDA Graphs are captured.
setup_work.retained_memory: Folded weight copies total 11,171,008 float32 elements (~44.7 MB) plus 20 folded bias vectors (2,752 floats, ~11 KB), retained in closures for the candidate lifetime on the CUDA device alongside the untouched originals (~44.7 MB). framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes therefore rise by roughly the folded-copy size (setup/installation allocation, reported here, not hidden); framework.peak_allocated_bytes is reset per run but still reflects these steady-state live allocations during the forward, so the offline row's peak_allocated_bytes memory goal may report a slightly higher peak (activation buffers dominate the run peak). This counter increase is the accounting cost of retaining a folded copy, not a physical-memory saving claim; the request's latency_ms objective carries no memory constraint (the 0.95 images_per_second ratio belongs to the offline row's memory goal, and throughput improves with latency).

quality_risks: Fold rounding vs assert_close(atol=rtol=1e-4) and require_exact_top1: reported CPU pre-validation shows max_abs_err=7.6e-6 with a 0.1446 minimum top1-top2 margin, but cuDNN may pick a different conv algorithm for bias-bearing folded weights on GPU, shifting the error; only the framework's independent GPU validation of the full logits and exact top-1 against the reference confirms fidelity.

Negative control (reference+1 corruption must stay rejected) operates on reference logits in the harness; both reference and actual forwards use the same replaced path with identical, bit-stable folded parameters, so the check remains well defined and passing, but it is re-verified rather than assumed.

Realized latency gain may be smaller than the removed 428.5us of aten::batch_norm leaf time if folded conv kernels (bias epilogue, possibly different cuDNN algorithm choice with cudnn.benchmark=False heuristics) run slower than the bias-free originals.

peak_allocated_bytes for the offline memory goal rises by roughly the ~44.7 MB retained folded copies (steady-state live allocation visible per run); no latency constraint is attached, and the 0.95 throughput ratio is unaffected, but the memory goal value itself will not improve.

Any replacement that hits its guard (unexpected signature/state, grad enabled, training flag) falls back to the unmodified parent for that call, which stays numerically correct but forfeits that site's speedup; fallback occurrences are visible through record_route labels and runtime coverage.
